method.description: Design reconciliation of one identity against the statute that creates the remedy. The question asked was not whether a binary could be obtained but whether a participant-completable document is required to exist at all, and the answer is settled by the statute's own prescription of who signs the application and on whose letterhead it must appear.
method.controllingSource: Fla. Stat. § 943.0581, Administrative expunction for arrests made contrary to law or by mistake, read in full at flsenate.gov
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition requires preserving the exact not-required reason, including custom pleading versus no participant filing, and forbids collapsing it into source missing or altering an adopted strategy. The reason is recorded at the precise branch the stop condition names — no participant filing — and is evidenced from the statute rather than inferred.

finding.headline: Administrative expunction is not a participant filing. The statute requires the application to be on the submitting agency's letterhead and signed by the head of that agency, so there is no document a participant can complete, and no form for this programme to acquire or generate.
finding.notRequiredReasonBasis: the statute's own prescription of the application's form and signatory, quoted verbatim below
finding.acquisitionRequiredRationale: No issuer interaction can produce a participant-completable form for a remedy whose application must be executed by a law enforcement agency on its own letterhead.
finding.isThisCustomPleadingWhy: A custom pleading is something this programme drafts for a participant to file. Here the participant files nothing at all — the filing is made by an agency, and a drafted document would be an agency's letter that the participant has no standing to issue.

statutoryBasis.heading: Administrative expunction for arrests made contrary to law or by mistake
statutoryBasis.implementingRule: Fla. Admin. Code R. 11C-7.008, Administrative Expunction, effective 2009-04-16

whoApplies.subsection2Verbatim: A law enforcement agency shall apply to the department in the manner prescribed by rule for the administrative expunction of any nonjudicial record of any arrest of a minor or an adult who is subsequently determined by the agency, at its discretion, or by the final order of a court of competent jurisdiction, to have been arrested contrary to law or by mistake.
whoApplies.subsection2Reading: The primary applicant is the arresting agency, and its duty is expressed as 'shall apply'.

theIndividualRoute.subsection3Verbatim: An adult or, in the case of a minor child, the parent or legal guardian of the minor child, may apply to the department in the manner prescribed by rule for the administrative expunction of any nonjudicial record of an arrest alleged to have been made contrary to law or by mistake, provided that the application is supported by the endorsement of the head of the arresting agency or his or her designee or the state attorney of the judicial circuit in which the arrest occurred or his or her designee.
theIndividualRoute.subsection3Reading: An individual may apply, but only with an endorsement the individual cannot supply. The endorsement must come from the head of the arresting agency or the state attorney. This looks at first like a participant route and is not one: the operative document still depends on a third party's signature.
theIndividualRoute.whyThisIsTheTrap: Read alone, subsection (3) would support modelling a participant-facing application. Subsection (4) forecloses it.

theDecisiveProvision.subsection4Verbatim: An application for administrative expunction shall include the date and time of the arrest, the name of the person arrested, the offender-based tracking system (OBTS) number, and the crime or crimes charged. The application shall be on the submitting agency's letterhead and shall be signed by the head of the submitting agency or his or her designee.
theDecisiveProvision.reading: The application must physically be on an agency's letterhead and must carry an agency head's signature. Both are attributes a participant cannot supply and this programme cannot generate. Whatever route subsection (3) contemplates, the instrument itself is an agency document.

warrantRoute.subsection5Verbatim: If the person was arrested on a warrant, capias, or pickup order, a request for an administrative expunction may be made by the sheriff of the county in which the warrant, capias, or pickup order was issued or his or her designee or by the state attorney of the judicial circuit in which the warrant, capias, or pickup order was issued or his or her designee.
warrantRoute.reading: A third applicant class, and again not the participant.

statutoryBasis.consequence: Every route to administrative expunction runs through a document executed by a public body. There is no participant-completable form, and there never was one to acquire.

resolvedIdentity.recordedRoleAssessment: primary_filing is wrong for a participant packet. It is a primary filing of the agency's, not the participant's. The role is right about the document's function in the proceeding and wrong about who performs it.
resolvedIdentity.documentExistsDetail: An application for administrative expunction plainly exists — the statute prescribes its required contents. What does not exist is a participant-completable published form, which is what the acquisition key implies.
resolvedIdentity.signatory: the head of the submitting law enforcement agency or their designee
resolvedIdentity.issuer: Florida Department of Law Enforcement receives it; the arresting agency, sheriff or state attorney authors it
resolvedIdentity.scopeBasis: a single statewide FDLE remedy under Chapter 943, not inferred from any address

distinguishedFromTheSiblingFdleJob.consequence: Florida has five FDLE-stage remedies and only four participant forms. The fifth is not a missing form; it is a remedy that does not use one.

notRequiredReasonPreserved.notCustomPleading: Expressly not. Drafting an agency letter for a participant would produce a document the participant cannot sign and cannot put on the required letterhead, and would misrepresent who is applying.
notRequiredReasonPreserved.notSourceMissing: Expressly not, and the stop condition forbids that collapse. The remedy exists, the application exists, and the statute prescribes its contents. Nothing is missing — the document simply is not the participant's.
notRequiredReasonPreserved.notAPhantomIdentity: Distinguish this from FL-RULE-3.989-CONTINUATION, resolved elsewhere in this programme, which named a document nobody publishes. Here a real application exists and is made by a real party; the defect is that the identity is bound to a participant component.
notRequiredReasonPreserved.whatTheParticipantCanDo: Under subsection (3) an adult may apply if they first obtain the endorsement of the arresting agency head or the state attorney. Obtaining that endorsement is a real-world action, not a document this programme generates. Whether the packet should explain that route in guidance is a legal-design question and is not decided here.
notRequiredReasonPreserved.adoptedStrategyUnchanged: The track's output strategy is untouched. Reclassifying fl-administrative is a legal-design decision, and this record supplies the source-side fact it would rest on.

sourceAvailabilityAndStructure.binaryExistsDetail: No participant-completable form file exists. FDLE publishes no administrative-expunction application form, and Rule 11C-7.008 incorporates none by reference — unlike the four sibling rules, each of which incorporates a numbered FDLE form with a flrules.org Ref id.
sourceAvailabilityAndStructure.whyAllNull: There is no document to measure. Recording measurements would be inventing them.
sourceAvailabilityAndStructure.sourceContractEligibleWhy: A source contract pins a document. There is no participant document to pin.
sourceAvailabilityAndStructure.materializationEligibleWhy: Materialization presupposes bytes. None exist and no receipt should ever be written for this identity.

doNotSubstitute.why: The Application for a Certificate of Eligibility for Sealing or Expunction, Ref-14423, revised June 2021. It is the participant application for the court-route remedies and is the single most likely wrong pick, because it is the FDLE form a reader will find when searching for an FDLE expunction application.
The lawful self-defense application under § 943.0578. A different statute, a different remedy, and participant-completed where this one is not.
The juvenile diversion and early juvenile applications. Both participant-completed.

doNotSubstitute.documentClass: the FDLE online intake portal output
doNotSubstitute.why: The portal covers the five request types and generates an unnumbered PDF. It is not the FAC-incorporated document for any remedy and it is not an agency letterhead application.

doNotSubstitute.documentClass: a county or arresting-agency local expunction request form
doNotSubstitute.why: Some agencies publish their own internal request forms. Those are agency instruments, not statewide participant forms, and must not be promoted to statewide on the strength of this record.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not source_missing, which the stop condition forbids and which would be false — the application exists and the statute prescribes its contents. It is not custom_pleading, the other branch the stop condition names, because a drafted document could not be signed or issued by the participant. It is not a phantom identity, because a real instrument exists. The precise fact is that the instrument is an agency's, and that is the not-required reason.

expectedDownstreamEffect: Florida's administrative-expunction identity closes without acquisition and with its reason recorded at the exact branch the assignment distinguishes: no participant filing, because § 943.0581(4) requires the application to be on the submitting agency's letterhead and signed by the head of that agency. The subsection (3) individual route is recorded as the trap it is — an adult may apply, but only with an endorsement they cannot supply, and the instrument remains an agency document either way. The identity is distinguished from the four participant FDLE forms resolved by the sibling job, explaining why Chapter 11C-7 has five remedies and four forms. No binary is acquired, no receipt is created, nothing enters version control, no adopted strategy is altered, no component is rebound, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
